title: Oscar and the Gravity
premise: When gravity fails for nine seconds across the Kepler-442 system, terraformer Emrys Okafor's cargo hauler is caught in the anomaly and he wakes with a message encoded in his own bones — the last transmission from Earth, carrying proof that the war's founding grievance was manufactured. Hunted by both fleets and shadowed by Vess, an enemy pilot who defects to protect him, Emrys must reach the seed-vault station where the colonists' unborn generation sleeps. He delivers the truth at terrible cost: Vess dies holding the relay open, and Emrys chooses exile over heroism, planting Earth's final garden among people who will never know his name.
about_author: Rosalind Almeida is a former orbital-mechanics engineer who traded simulation software for fiction after a decade designing life-support systems no one ever thanked her for. She writes about people who maintain worlds they may never see finished.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Emrys Okafor, hauling soil cultures through contested orbits above the half-terraformed moon Verity, experiences the system-wide gravity flicker firsthand as his ship tumbles and every star seems to stutter. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine — a man who tends gardens for the unborn feels the universe itself betray its own constancy.

chapters.title: The Weight in His Bones
chapters.summary: Salvaged by a neutral medical barge, Emrys learns scans show an encoded structure woven into his skeleton during the flicker — Earth's last transmission loop, addressed to no one and everyone. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: violation and awe; his body is no longer only his, and the message hums when he dreams.

chapters.title: Vess Descending
chapters.summary: Coalition pilot Vess Arden intercepts Emrys under orders to capture him, but recognizes the transmission signature her dead brother died chasing rumors of. She lets him slip the net instead. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: duty cracking against grief; she burns her career in nine seconds of hesitation.

chapters.title: Cargo of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Emrys and Vess run dark through debris fields, decoding fragments: the war's casus belli — the alleged Coalition strike on Earth's ark fleet — was staged by Earth's own command. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: bitter intimacy grows between two people carrying incompatible loyalties in one small ship.

chapters.title: The Garden That Waits
chapters.summary: They shelter at Emrys's old terraforming station, where he shows Vess the seed vaults meant for generations not yet born. Coalition hunters arrive; the station burns. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: loss sharpened into resolve — he has already lost one garden to the war; he refuses to lose the message too.

chapters.title: What the Fleets Know
chapters.summary: A captured Coalition admiral reveals both sides' high commands have known the truth for years and fear it more than each other. The message must never land anywhere with an audience. POV: Vess. Emotional beat: disillusionment hardening into defiance — the conspiracy isn't one side's sin but the whole architecture's.

chapters.title: Orbit of Knives
chapters.summary: Both fleets converge on the seed-vault station Halcyon, where the sleeping colonists orbit like a held breath. Emrys and Vess thread the battle on a stolen tug, broadcasting decoys. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; every near-miss is a promise kept.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: At Halcyon, the transmission can only be released through a manually held relay while the fleets jam everything. Vess locks herself into the relay chamber as jamming fire tears the station apart. POV: Vess, then Emrys outside. Emotional beat: love stated plainly at last, in the language of sacrifice rather than words.

chapters.title: Truth at Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: The message plays across every open channel — and across the system, gravity flickers again for exactly nine seconds, as if the universe pauses to listen. Fleets go silent mid-battle. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph; the war ends not with victory but with shared, unbearable knowledge.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Gravity
chapters.summary: Refusing medals and tribunals alike, Emrys returns to the burned terraforming station and begins planting again, carrying Vess's name into the soil record so the waking colonists will inherit it. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: mourning folded into inheritance — survival was the price, and the garden is what it bought.
